meta.label: Music streaming
meta.attribution: Curated from public artist-payout disclosures, platform docs, licensing notes and privacy policies - not audited figures. Per-stream payouts vary by deal, country and rightsholder chain. Every criterion has a cited basis; reviewed 2026-06. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Bandcamp
products.description: An artist-first marketplace where fans stream, buy, and download music with a much larger share going to artists and labels than passive streaming.

artist_pay.note: Bandcamp says its share is 15% on digital items and 10% on physical goods, with usually 80-85% going to the artist or label.

openness.note: Bandcamp is an online record store where fans directly support artists and can buy downloadable music and physical goods.

privacy.note: Bandcamp's 2025 privacy policy discloses purchase/account data and consent-based ad tracking rather than a pure surveillance-feed model.

catalog.note: Strong for independent artists and labels, but not a complete substitute for major-label streaming catalogs.

accessibility.note: Free to browse and preview, but durable ownership/support comes from buying music or merch.

products.name: Buy directly / physical (vinyl, CDs)
products.description: The old-fashioned high-leverage route: buy records, merch, or DRM-free files from artists and labels you want to support.

artist_pay.note: Bandcamp says artists receive 82% on average and that its revenue share is 15% for digital music and 10% for merch.

openness.note: Bandcamp lets buyers download purchases in their preferred audio format, giving more control than streaming-only access.

privacy.note: Direct purchases avoid an always-on streaming profile, though Bandcamp still processes account and purchase data under its terms.

catalog.note: Catalog access is limited to what you choose to buy or download, even when a store also offers app-based listening.

accessibility.note: Direct buying has per-release costs rather than a flat subscription, but Bandcamp still supports apps and high-quality downloads.

products.name: Artist memberships (Patreon)
products.description: A recurring membership route for artists who share music, demos, posts, tickets, or community access directly with supporters.

artist_pay.note: Patreon lists creator platform fees from 8% to 12% plus payment processing, making it a clearer direct-support channel than pooled streaming.

openness.note: Membership posts and audio can be valuable direct access, but they are hosted inside Patreon's account/payment platform rather than a DRM-free catalog.

privacy.note: Patreon's creator privacy promise describes member data responsibilities, but the platform still processes account, payment and membership data.

catalog.note: Not a broad music catalog: it works when the artist you already care about offers a membership.

accessibility.note: Creator-set memberships can be affordable, but access depends on each artist's tiers and payment setup.

products.name: Resonate

artist_pay.note: Resonate's co-op model was artist/listener aligned, but the official site now says the co-op has been dissolved and is closing out finances.

openness.note: Historically open/cooperative, but the live service is no longer operating as a normal streaming option.

privacy.note: member co-op, low tracking

catalog.note: The catalog is effectively unavailable as a current consumer streaming choice after dissolution.

accessibility.note: Not a practical current recommendation: official site says the co-op has been dissolved.

products.description: A once-promising cooperative stream-to-own platform; as of 2026 its official site says the co-op has dissolved.

products.name: Mirlo
products.description: An open-source, collectively managed music sales and patronage platform built as a Bandcamp-like alternative.

artist_pay.note: direct artist sales and patronage; artists can set the platform share down to zero

openness.note: open-source audio distribution and patronage platform

privacy.note: small direct-support platform without ad-scale profiling

catalog.note: very small catalog compared with mainstream streaming

accessibility.note: usable web marketplace, but still niche and early

products.name: Jamendo
products.description: A free independent-music platform built around legal streaming/downloads and commercial licensing for artists.

artist_pay.note: licensing arm shares revenue with independent artists, but free listening is not direct purchase support

openness.note: music is published under Creative Commons licenses chosen by artists

privacy.note: standard web platform rather than ad-mega-platform

catalog.note: 600,000+ free songs from 40,000+ independent artists

accessibility.note: free streaming and downloads for personal use

products.name: Audius
products.description: A decentralized, open-source music platform that gives artists direct distribution tools, with web3 tradeoffs.

artist_pay.note: artist-controlled protocol with monetization tools, but revenue model is less proven than direct sales

openness.note: open-source apps and open music protocol documentation

privacy.note: social/blockchain-style platform exposes more public activity than private listening

catalog.note: large for creator uploads, but not a full major-label catalog

accessibility.note: free streaming and uploading with web/mobile apps

products.name: Public library (hoopla / Freegal)
products.description: A free-with-library-card route for music access through services such as Hoopla or Freegal, with local availability limits.

artist_pay.note: your library licenses & pays for access

openness.note: some downloads DRM-free

privacy.note: library privacy norms (varies)

catalog.note: decent, rotates

accessibility.note: free with a library card

products.name: NTS Radio
products.description: A free, ad-free global radio platform centered on resident DJs, leftfield discovery, and curated archives rather than algorithmic playlists.

artist_pay.note: NTS says it pays royalties for aired music and pays resident hosts through Supporter subscriptions.

openness.note: Free streaming and show archives, but not a DRM-free download store or user-owned catalog.

privacy.note: Ad-free radio avoids ad-targeting incentives, though it remains a standard web/app service.

catalog.note: Broad curated radio platform with hundreds of resident hosts, strongest for discovery rather than on-demand mainstream catalog breadth.

accessibility.note: NTS is free, ad-free, and streams live 24/7 online.

products.name: SomaFM
products.description: A long-running, listener-supported, commercial-free internet radio network with human-curated niche channels.

artist_pay.note: SomaFM is listener-supported and licensed to broadcast, but it is radio access rather than direct artist purchase support.

openness.note: Free streams are easy to access, but SomaFM says it is licensed only to broadcast and cannot provide downloads.

privacy.note: SomaFM's privacy policy says it will not sell, rent, or abuse listener email or postal addresses.

catalog.note: SomaFM offers over 30 hand-picked underground/alternative radio channels, strong for discovery but not on-demand catalog breadth.

accessibility.note: Free web streams are available through popup players and standard AAC/MP3 stream links.

products.name: Mixcloud
products.description: A licensed platform for DJ mixes, radio shows, and long-form music programming, with creator subscriptions and rights-holder licensing.

artist_pay.note: Creator Subscriptions route revenue to creators after royalties, rights-holder fees, and transaction costs.

openness.note: Licensed streaming model enables legal mixes but restricts unrestricted on-demand access and downloads.

privacy.note: Standard commercial web/app account model with creator and listener analytics rather than a local/private library.

catalog.note: Strong for DJ mixes, radio shows, and long-form creator uploads; weaker as an all-purpose album catalog.

accessibility.note: Mixcloud offers free listening with paid creator subscriptions and Pro features.

products.name: Internet Archive Live Music Archive
products.description: A nonprofit public archive of live concert recordings from trade-friendly artists, focused on preservation and free access.

artist_pay.note: Archive hosts royalty-free, no-cost downloads from trade-friendly artists; it preserves access more than it directly pays musicians.

openness.note: Live recordings are available for no-cost public streaming/downloads where artists allow noncommercial distribution.

privacy.note: Public web archive model with optional accounts creates less music-profile lock-in than mainstream streaming subscriptions.

catalog.note: Large archive for live recordings, but intentionally narrow compared with mainstream on-demand music catalogs.

accessibility.note: Internet Archive describes the collection as a free public library of live recordings.

products.name: Free Music Archive
products.description: A free music discovery and download archive for legal independent music, strongest when open access matters more than direct artist income.

artist_pay.note: Free Music Archive emphasizes free legal access; it is better for discovery/open culture than for direct payment to musicians.

openness.note: Creative Commons describes FMA as an interactive library of high-quality, legal audio downloads using CC-style open sharing.

privacy.note: The archive is free to access on the web and does not require a streaming subscription account for basic discovery.

catalog.note: Best for independent and openly licensed music discovery, not a full major-label catalog substitute.

accessibility.note: Free web access and downloadable tracks make it one of the easiest open-music routes.

products.name: Musopen
products.description: A nonprofit public-domain music commons for free classical recordings, sheet music, radio, and education materials.

artist_pay.note: Musopen is a nonprofit access commons, so it is strong for public culture but not a current-artist payout channel.

openness.note: Musopen provides recordings, sheet music, and textbooks for free without copyright restrictions.

privacy.note: Musopen has a simple account/privacy policy rather than an ad-scale streaming profile model.

catalog.note: Musopen focuses on public-domain music and asks users to verify public-domain status, so breadth is intentionally narrower than mainstream catalogs.

accessibility.note: Free music recordings, sheet music, radio, apps, and educational materials make access broad for classical and learning use.

products.name: Self-hosted owned library (Navidrome / Jellyfin)
products.description: A self-hosted path for streaming music you already own from your own server, using open-source tools instead of a rented catalog.

artist_pay.note: Artist support depends on how the files were acquired; best when paired with direct purchases or DRM-free stores.

openness.note: Navidrome is open-source GPL software; Jellyfin is a free software media system for your own server.

privacy.note: Self-hosting keeps playback and library control on your own server rather than a platform profile.

catalog.note: Catalog is limited to the files you own or import, with no built-in mainstream streaming catalog.

accessibility.note: Powerful but technical: you must run your own server and manage files, clients, backups, and access.

products.name: SiriusXM
products.description: A paid satellite/app radio service with curated music channels, strong reach in cars, and royalty payments through statutory digital-radio structures.

artist_pay.note: SiriusXM says its music royalty fee supports copyright royalties to recording artists, musicians and labels for sound recordings.

openness.note: SiriusXM is a subscription radio/app service rather than user-owned DRM-free music.

privacy.note: SiriusXM's 2026 privacy policy covers consumer websites, apps and services across SiriusXM and Pandora subsidiaries.

catalog.note: All Access includes ad-free music by genre, decade, artist and mood plus sports, news, talk and podcasts.

accessibility.note: SiriusXM is widely available in cars and apps, but full access is subscription-based after promotions.

products.name: iHeartRadio
products.description: A free-to-start commercial radio, podcast and music app with major broadcast-radio reach and paid on-demand upgrades.

artist_pay.note: SoundExchange says it collects statutory digital-performance royalties from platforms including iHeartRadio.

openness.note: iHeartRadio is a licensed streaming and radio service; offline listening and on-demand use sit inside paid app access.

privacy.note: iHeart's 2026 privacy notice covers processing across websites, apps, services, ads and interactive features.

catalog.note: All Access offers on-demand playback, playlists, offline listening and a library of millions of songs.

accessibility.note: iHeartRadio offers free radio, music and podcasts with paid upgrades for on-demand and offline listening.

products.name: TuneIn
products.description: A global live-radio, sports, news and podcast aggregator, useful for discovery but not a direct artist-support or ownership model.

artist_pay.note: For internet radio, creator payment generally flows through statutory digital-performance and station licensing rather than direct fan support.

openness.note: TuneIn aggregates radio streams and premium stations; it does not provide owned DRM-free music downloads.

privacy.note: TuneIn publishes a privacy policy for personal data processing across its app and service.

catalog.note: TuneIn brings together live sports, music, news, audiobooks and podcasts, with premium music/news options.

accessibility.note: The app is free for broad station access, with optional TuneIn Premium for commercial-free music/news and sports.

products.name: Live365
products.description: An internet-radio platform for independent stations, with built-in licensing coverage and free listening to thousands of human-run streams.

artist_pay.note: Live365 says its standard broadcaster packages include music licensing and royalty reporting for the United States, Mexico and Canada.

openness.note: Live365 lets independent broadcasters create online stations, but listener access is still station streaming rather than owned files.

privacy.note: Live365 publishes a privacy policy and a CCPA notice; its CCPA notice says some personal information may be sold to third parties.

catalog.note: Live365 describes itself as a place to discover thousands of stations from many music and talk styles.

accessibility.note: Listeners can discover stations through the Live365 website and apps, while broadcasters pay for station packages.

products.name: Radio Garden
products.description: A simple global radio map for live stations around the world, excellent for discovery but dependent on station-level licensing and availability.

artist_pay.note: Radio Garden is a station gateway; payment to creators depends on the underlying broadcaster and internet-radio licensing path.

openness.note: Radio Garden lets listeners tune into live stations worldwide by location rather than locking them into one proprietary catalog.

privacy.note: Radio Garden publishes a privacy policy explaining collection, use and disclosure of personal data for the service.

catalog.note: The app description says each green dot represents a city or town and that new stations are added regularly.

accessibility.note: Radio Garden is free and browser/app based, though station availability can vary by country and licensing limits.

products.name: BBC Sounds
products.description: A UK public-service audio app for BBC radio, music mixes and podcasts, strong on ad-free access but geographically limited.

artist_pay.note: BBC Sounds is public-broadcaster audio, so artist support is licensing and commissioning rather than direct fan purchase.

openness.note: BBC Sounds streams and downloads BBC audio inside BBC-controlled apps and website rather than offering user-owned music files.

privacy.note: The BBC Sounds app privacy notice explains BBC account, usage and personalization data handling.

catalog.note: BBC Sounds brings BBC radio, podcasts and music together, but it is not an all-label on-demand music catalog.

accessibility.note: BBC Sounds is free and ad-free for UK use, with international access constrained by BBC availability and rights rules.

products.name: KEXP
products.description: A nonprofit, listener-supported music-discovery station with human curation, live sessions, and open streaming URLs.

artist_pay.note: KEXP says listener support lets decisions be guided by mission and music discovery rather than ratings or profit.

openness.note: KEXP publishes live streaming URLs that work with third-party players such as VLC, Apple Music, Spotify and Sonos.

privacy.note: KEXP's 2025 privacy policy covers website, app and communications data collection for its nonprofit services.

catalog.note: KEXP is a curated station and arts organization, not an on-demand catalog of mainstream music.

accessibility.note: KEXP streams live online and through apps, with free access supported by listeners and donors.

products.name: Anghami
products.description: A major Middle East and North Africa streaming service with Arabic and international music, a free tier, and paid Plus plans.

artist_pay.note: Anghami has artist tools and label/distributor routes, but ordinary listening remains a licensed streaming model rather than direct purchase.

openness.note: Anghami Plus offers unlimited downloads and ad-free listening inside the service, not owned DRM-free files.

privacy.note: Anghami's legal page says it uses personal and usage data to provide and improve the service.

catalog.note: Anghami investor materials describe more than 70 million users and over 57 million Arabic and international songs.

accessibility.note: Anghami offers free listening plus paid Plus and family plans with downloads, no ads and higher audio quality.

products.name: Boomplay
products.description: A large Africa-focused streaming app with strong regional catalog breadth, free access, and unresolved royalty-trust concerns.

artist_pay.note: Sony Music removed its catalog from Boomplay in 2024 amid reported unpaid-royalty disputes, limiting the artist-pay score.

openness.note: Boomplay is an app-based freemium streaming and download service rather than an owned DRM-free music store.

privacy.note: Boomplay's app-store disclosures indicate app data practices may vary and that the app collects user data for service features.

catalog.note: Boomplay's store listing says the service has over 100 million songs across many genres and podcasts.

accessibility.note: Boomplay markets free streaming, downloads and offline play, with strong accessibility in its focus markets.

products.name: JioSaavn
products.description: A major Indian music and podcast streaming app with a large regional-language catalog, free listening, and paid Pro features.

artist_pay.note: JioSaavn's Artist Dashboard gives artists streaming, audience and performance insights, but payment still flows through labels/aggregators.

openness.note: JioSaavn Pro adds ad-free and offline listening inside the app rather than user-owned DRM-free downloads.

privacy.note: JioSaavn Artist Dashboard uses listener data and audience insights for artists and managers, so privacy is a mainstream platform tradeoff.

catalog.note: The Google Play listing describes an 8 crore-plus song library across 16 languages plus podcasts.

accessibility.note: JioSaavn is free with ads, with Pro adding no ads, downloads, offline listening and higher-quality audio.

products.name: Tidal
products.description: A paid hi-fi streaming service with artist tools, direct-to-fan sales for eligible uploads, and a broad catalog, but still mostly a rented streaming model.

artist_pay.note: TIDAL has artist-facing tools and direct-to-fan sales for eligible uploads, but standard royalty reporting still flows through distributors or labels.

openness.note: Main catalog use is licensed streaming, though eligible uploaded albums/tracks can now be sold directly to fans.

privacy.note: TIDAL's 2026 privacy notice lists account, subscription, usage, playback, search, login and device data processing.

catalog.note: TIDAL markets more than 110 million songs in HiFi sound quality.

accessibility.note: Current US pricing is paid subscription plus free trial; individual, family and student plans are listed.

products.name: Qobuz
products.description: An audiophile-leaning paid service with published average payout data, a hi-res download store, and more ownership than streaming-only apps.

artist_pay.note: Qobuz says an independent audit confirmed average 2024 royalties of US$0.01873 per stream to labels and publishers, who then pay artists under contracts.

openness.note: Qobuz pairs streaming with a Hi-Res/CD-quality download store, improving ownership compared with streaming-only services.

privacy.note: Qobuz's personal-data page describes subscription, usage, cookies and service-improvement processing under Xandrie.

catalog.note: Qobuz says it offers more than 100 million tracks for streaming.

accessibility.note: Paid-only model with free trial; US plan page lists annual and monthly pricing.

products.name: Presto Music
products.description: A specialist classical and jazz service with CD-quality streaming, high-resolution downloads, and a pay-per-second streaming model.

artist_pay.note: Presto says its streaming royalties are paid by playtime, not track count, to avoid short tracks diluting longer classical works.

openness.note: Presto offers purchased digital downloads alongside streaming, including lossless and high-resolution options where available.

privacy.note: The Android app listing reports collection of personal info and app activity, with data not shared with third parties.

catalog.note: Presto says its streaming service offers around 200,000 classical and jazz albums, strong in niche depth rather than all-purpose breadth.

accessibility.note: The service is paid and region-limited, available in the UK, US, Canada, Australia/New Zealand and about 30 European countries.

products.name: IDAGIO
products.description: A classical-specialist streaming service with work-aware search, expert curation, a free radio mode, and paid on-demand plans.

artist_pay.note: IDAGIO is a licensed streaming service, but it does not publish a direct artist-centric payout rate like Qobuz or Bandcamp.

openness.note: Free access is radio-style; on-demand, offline listening, and lossless audio sit behind subscriptions rather than DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: IDAGIO support says it requires an email address and will not share personal information with third parties.

catalog.note: IDAGIO says it has a catalogue of over 2 million licensed classical tracks with search tailored for classical works.

accessibility.note: IDAGIO offers a free tier plus paid plans, though full on-demand and offline features require subscription.

products.name: Beatport
products.description: A DJ-focused electronic and open-format music store where buying tracks can matter more than passive streaming.

artist_pay.note: publishes high average streaming payout claims and supports paid downloads through labels/distributors

openness.note: downloaded tracks can be kept; streaming subscriptions remain locked to DJ software

privacy.note: standard commercial music-service account and purchase data

catalog.note: millions of tracks across 40+ DJ/electronic and open-format genres

accessibility.note: paid downloads/streaming; strongest for DJs, less useful for casual listeners

products.name: SoundCloud
products.description: A creator-upload platform with fan-powered royalties and strong discovery for emerging artists, alongside standard streaming tradeoffs.

artist_pay.note: SoundCloud's fan-powered royalties direct listener revenue toward the artists a fan actually streams.

openness.note: DRM streaming; open uploads

privacy.note: standard tracking

catalog.note: huge for emerging/indie

accessibility.note: free tier + paid

products.name: Audiomack
products.description: A free, creator-upload streaming and discovery platform with monetization for eligible artists and strong mobile access.

artist_pay.note: Audiomack Monetization Program lets eligible creators earn money and receive payouts from streams.

openness.note: Creators can upload limitless music and podcasts, but listener access is still a platform streaming model rather than DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: Audiomack says its ad-supported free listening model is designed around minimum data collection and anonymous advertisers.

catalog.note: On-demand creator uploads and free limitless artist uploads make it broad for emerging and regional scenes, not a full major-label substitute.

accessibility.note: Free listening and mobile/web access make it easy to use, with monetization funded partly by advertising.

products.name: iTunes Store downloads
products.description: A mainstream buy-to-own route for downloadable music files, useful when you want ownership without using a niche store.

artist_pay.note: Purchased music creates a specific paid sale through Apple's music storefront, though the source does not disclose artist/label splits.

openness.note: Apple says iTunes Plus songs are DRM-free 256 kbps AAC files after upgrade or purchase where available.

privacy.note: Apple's privacy policy covers media purchases and account data, but the model is less ad-driven than free streaming.

catalog.note: The iTunes Store remains a large mainstream music-purchase channel, but it is not the same as a complete streaming catalog.

accessibility.note: Apple documents buying and redownloading iTunes Store music across Apple devices and Windows.

products.name: Apple Music
products.description: A paid mainstream service with strong catalog and Apple privacy posture, but no DRM-free ownership.

artist_pay.note: Apple's artist page says individual paid plans averaged about $0.01 per play in 2020, including label and publisher royalties.

openness.note: Apple Music is subscription streaming; access is not DRM-free ownership of the catalog.

privacy.note: Apple's stated privacy stance

catalog.note: Apple Music is a mainstream paid catalog service, though the cited royalty page is about payout policy rather than exact catalog size.

accessibility.note: Paid-only long-term use, with especially smooth access on Apple devices.

products.name: Deezer
products.description: A mainstream streaming platform experimenting with artist-centric royalty rules while remaining a standard licensed-access service.

artist_pay.note: Deezer documents an Artist-Centric Payment System intended to reward engaged listening and reduce low-value noise/fraud.

openness.note: Deezer is licensed streaming; offline downloads are a paid-plan feature rather than DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: Deezer treats listening history, favorite content, searches, product interaction and advertising data as personal data.

catalog.note: Deezer says it provides access to over 120 million tracks worldwide.

accessibility.note: Deezer offers a free ad-supported tier plus paid plans with offline listening.

products.name: Amazon Music
products.description: A large streaming catalog tied into Amazon's wider account and Prime ecosystem.

artist_pay.note: Amazon Music for Artists says Amazon pays rightsholders, who then distribute royalties according to their artist agreements.

openness.note: Amazon Music is licensed streaming access; catalog listening is not DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: Amazon's privacy notice covers account, usage, advertising, device and purchasing data across Amazon services.

catalog.note: Amazon says Music Unlimited has over 100 million songs in HD, while Prime members get access to 100 million songs ad-free.

accessibility.note: Amazon Music combines Prime-bundled access, Unlimited on-demand access, and a free ad-supported experience in selected countries.

products.name: YouTube Music
products.description: A highly accessible music layer on YouTube's ad and account ecosystem, strong on catalog but weak on privacy and ownership.

artist_pay.note: YouTube said it paid the music industry over $8B from July 2024-June 2025 through ads plus subscriptions, but this is still rights-holder payout rather than direct artist purchase.

openness.note: YouTube Music is licensed streaming tied to Google's platform, not DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: Google privacy policy covers YouTube/YouTube Music account, activity and ad-personalization data.

catalog.note: YouTube cites more than 2 billion logged-in monthly music-video viewers alongside its subscription base.

accessibility.note: Large free/ad-supported access plus paid Music/Premium subscriptions make it highly accessible.

products.name: Pandora
products.description: A U.S.-only personalized radio and on-demand streaming service with strong ease of use, ad support, and standard platform privacy tradeoffs.

artist_pay.note: Pandora offers artist AMP tools and distributor onboarding, but listener revenue still flows through platform/rightsholder licensing rather than direct purchases.

openness.note: Pandora Premium and Plus are licensed streaming/offline access services, not DRM-free music ownership.

privacy.note: The Android listing reports third-party sharing and collection of location, personal information, and other data types.

catalog.note: Pandora's AMP playbook says its catalog expansion gives listeners access to over 10 million unique artists.

accessibility.note: Pandora has a free ad-supported app plus Plus and Premium subscriptions, but the app listing says availability is U.S.-only.

products.name: Spotify
products.description: The default global streaming app for many listeners, excellent on catalog and convenience but structurally weak for artist income and ownership.

artist_pay.note: Spotify says it uses streamshare rather than a fixed per-stream rate, and artist royalties vary by market and label/distributor agreements.

openness.note: Spotify is a licensed streaming-access service; offline listening is not user-owned DRM-free music.

privacy.note: Spotify privacy policy covers personalization, usage data and advertising/measurement data processing.

catalog.note: Spotify's Loud & Clear says it analyzed 2025 royalty data and explains how money flows through the streaming economy.

accessibility.note: Broad global availability and a large free tier make Spotify one of the easiest mainstream services to adopt.

products.name: Radio Paradise
products.description: A human-curated, commercial-free internet radio option with excellent ease and audio quality, but no ownership or on-demand catalog.

artist_pay.note: Radio Paradise is listener-supported and commercial-free, but it is still radio-style listening rather than direct artist purchase.

openness.note: Radio Paradise streams curated channels; it does not give listeners DRM-free ownership of the music.

privacy.note: The iOS App Store privacy label says Radio Paradise collects usage and diagnostic data not linked to the user.

catalog.note: The catalog is broad for human-curated radio across rock, world, electronica, jazz and classical touches, but not an all-music search catalog.

accessibility.note: Radio Paradise offers free, no-ad streaming with no subscription fees through web and apps.

products.name: WFMU
products.description: A listener-supported freeform radio institution with deep archives and strong privacy signals, best for discovery rather than choosing exact albums.

artist_pay.note: WFMU is listener-supported and non-commercial, supporting music discovery without ad-driven platform economics, though it is not direct artist purchase.

openness.note: WFMU offers live streams, web-only channels, archives and podcasts, but not DRM-free ownership of the underlying music.

privacy.note: WFMU's privacy policy describes limited information collection, and the iOS app listing says the app does not collect data.

catalog.note: WFMU has a broad freeform schedule, web-only channels, archives and podcasts, but it is curated radio rather than a full on-demand catalog.

accessibility.note: WFMU streams free online and through mobile apps, with no paid subscription required.

products.name: dublab
products.description: A nonprofit, listener-powered radio station for independent and experimental music discovery.

artist_pay.note: dublab is a listener-powered nonprofit station and says memberships support station operations and archives.

openness.note: dublab is streaming/community radio rather than downloadable music ownership.

privacy.note: dublab's web model is lighter than ad-tech music platforms, though membership/newsletter tools still collect user information.

catalog.note: The station is strong for independent, experimental and cultural programming, but it is not a mainstream all-catalog streaming service.

accessibility.note: dublab streams freely online, with optional donations and memberships.

products.name: The Lot Radio
products.description: A 24/7 independent online station from Brooklyn, strongest for DJ culture and human-curated discovery.

artist_pay.note: The Lot Radio is an independent nonprofit online station; it supports scenes and selectors, but is not a direct artist-sales channel.

openness.note: The Lot Radio streams and archives station programming but does not provide owned music files.

privacy.note: The Lot Radio publishes a current privacy policy explaining collection and use of visitor and registered-user information.

catalog.note: The catalog is a continuous curated stream of NYC and international DJ programming, not searchable all-music access.

accessibility.note: The station streams free 24/7 online and through apps, supported by donations, merch and its kiosk model.

products.name: KCRW Music
products.description: A public-radio music discovery option with free live and app streams, especially useful for curated listening rather than ownership.

artist_pay.note: KCRW is a listener/member-supported public radio station and music-discovery platform, though it is not direct artist purchase.

openness.note: KCRW offers live and on-demand music channels through its app and site, but not DRM-free owned music.

privacy.note: KCRW publishes an online privacy policy describing collected information and disclosure practices.

catalog.note: KCRW is strong for curated music discovery, original shows and free on-demand music channels, but not a comprehensive catalog service.

accessibility.note: KCRW is available free via web and app, with local FM reach and worldwide streaming.

products.name: BeatStars
products.description: A beat marketplace where producers set licenses and prices directly, useful for creators buying production rather than casual listening.

artist_pay.note: BeatStars says producers manage their own licenses, pricing, sales and client communication, making it more artist/producer-directed than passive streaming.

openness.note: BeatStars sells licenses and files under producer-defined terms; ownership and usage rights vary by license rather than by platform-wide DRM-free ownership.

privacy.note: BeatStars' GDPR notice describes collection and use of personal data to provide services, process payments and customize the experience.

catalog.note: BeatStars describes itself as a music marketplace for buying, selling and giving away beats, with producers managing their own stores.

accessibility.note: BeatStars is easy to browse globally, but it serves creators buying/licensing beats rather than everyday streaming listeners.

products.name: HDtracks
products.description: A download-first option for people who want purchased high-resolution files rather than another rental-streaming subscription.

artist_pay.note: Download purchases create a clearer sale than passive streams, but HDtracks does not publish an artist/rightsholder split on its public store page.

openness.note: HDtracks describes itself as a high-resolution music platform for downloading tracks in master studio quality rather than a streaming-only rental service.

privacy.note: A download store creates less continuous listening telemetry after purchase than streaming, but purchases still require account/payment data.

catalog.note: HDtracks is strong for audiophile and hi-res releases, but it is not a full mainstream streaming catalog replacement.

accessibility.note: The store is useful for hi-res buyers, but purchased downloads are pricier and more file-management-heavy than mainstream streaming.

products.name: Bleep
products.description: An independent-music shop for digital downloads, vinyl, CDs, cassettes, merch, and curated label discovery.

artist_pay.note: Bleep works with labels and artists around the globe and sells music and merch, but it does not publish a Bandcamp-style artist split.

openness.note: Bleep says it sells vinyl, CDs, cassettes, digital files including 24-bit WAV, limited exclusives, and other formats.

privacy.note: A store purchase model is lighter than ad-supported listening, but Bleep still needs account, payment, and order data.

catalog.note: Bleep specializes in independent and innovative music across genre and format rather than all major-label catalog coverage.

accessibility.note: Bleep sells globally online, but it is more useful for intentional buyers than for free, frictionless streaming.

products.name: Boomkat
products.description: A specialist independent shop for vinyl, CDs, cassettes, and downloads, especially useful for deeper electronic, experimental, and archival music.

artist_pay.note: Boomkat is a specialist record store, so buying there supports a music retail ecosystem, though public artist/label split details are not posted.

openness.note: Boomkat says it supplies vinyl, CD, cassette, and download releases to customers in more than 100 countries.

privacy.note: Boomkat's privacy notice explains collected personal data and says it is committed to protecting and respecting privacy.

catalog.note: Boomkat is strong for independent, specialist, and underground releases, but not a universal mainstream streaming catalog.

accessibility.note: The store ships and sells downloads worldwide, but pricing, import shipping, and niche curation make it less casual than streaming.

products.name: Discogs Marketplace
products.description: A huge music database and marketplace for buying and selling vinyl, CDs, cassettes, and other physical releases.

artist_pay.note: Discogs is mainly a marketplace for buyers and sellers, so secondhand purchases support collectors and shops more directly than artists.

openness.note: The marketplace focuses on owned physical formats including vinyl, CDs, and cassettes rather than app-locked streams.

privacy.note: Discogs publishes privacy and data-protection documentation for its marketplace, apps, API, and related services.

catalog.note: Discogs describes itself as the largest online music database with a marketplace for records, CDs, cassettes, and more.

accessibility.note: Discogs is globally browsable, but condition grading, seller reliability, shipping, and collector prices add friction.

products.name: Ko-fi artist support
products.description: A lightweight way to tip, subscribe to, or buy from musicians and creators who maintain their own support pages.

artist_pay.note: Ko-fi says it uses creator-friendly 0-5% fees and no monthly fee, with tips, memberships, sales, and commissions available.

openness.note: Ko-fi can host creator shops and posts, but music/file ownership depends on how each artist configures their page.

privacy.note: Ko-fi says supporter payments require basic details and that payment processors may reveal some information to creators.

catalog.note: Ko-fi is not a music catalog; it is useful only when a specific artist or creator uses it.

accessibility.note: Supporters can make one-off tips, memberships, and shop purchases, making it an easy direct-support complement to streaming.

products.name: Bandzoogle artist stores
products.description: A musician website/storefront platform that lets artists sell music, merch, downloads, tickets, and fan subscriptions from their own sites.

artist_pay.note: Bandzoogle says artists can sell music and merch commission-free, including downloads, tickets, and band merchandise.

openness.note: Bandzoogle's music-selling tools support digital music downloads, so artists can offer owned files from their own sites.

privacy.note: Bandzoogle publishes a privacy policy and also lets artist sites add their own terms/privacy text, so privacy depends partly on the artist site setup.

catalog.note: Bandzoogle is artist infrastructure, not a discovery catalog; fans benefit only when an artist has built a site there.

accessibility.note: For fans, access depends on each artist's website; for artists, the platform provides templates and e-commerce tools.

products.name: Kickstarter Music
products.description: A project-funding route for albums, reissues, venues, performances, and other music work before it exists.

artist_pay.note: Kickstarter says music projects have attracted more than a million backers, and its music page includes albums, reissues, shows, and performances.

openness.note: Rewards can include downloads, physical media, tickets, or other artist-defined goods, but Kickstarter is not itself a DRM-free music library.

privacy.note: Kickstarter's privacy policy says it retains personal information as needed to provide services, so privacy is weaker than a simple cash-at-show purchase.

catalog.note: Kickstarter is a project marketplace, not a listening catalog; usefulness depends on active campaigns.

accessibility.note: Backing a project is easy online, but delivery timing, project risk, and all-or-nothing funding make it less immediate than buying existing music.

products.name: Resident Advisor
products.description: A global electronic-music guide for events, clubs, DJs, tickets, features, and scene discovery.

artist_pay.note: RA ticketing helps promoters sell tickets for clubs, festivals, and electronic music events, supporting live-music infrastructure rather than streaming royalties.

openness.note: Resident Advisor is an events, editorial, and ticketing platform, not a music ownership or download service.

privacy.note: RA's privacy policy explains that personal data supplied through its services may be processed by RA or on its behalf.

catalog.note: RA is strong for electronic music events, clubs, DJs, tickets, news, and rave culture, but not for all-genre catalog listening.

accessibility.note: RA provides global event discovery and ticketing, but its usefulness depends on geography and live-event budget.

products.name: Apple Music Classical
products.description: A dedicated classical-music app included with Apple Music, useful for metadata, search, and catalog depth but still part of the Apple Music rental ecosystem.

artist_pay.note: Apple Music Classical is included inside Apple Music rather than a direct-purchase model, so artist support follows the ordinary streaming-rights chain.

openness.note: The app syncs with Apple Music and requires an Apple Music subscription for full access, so it is not an owned-file or DRM-free route.

privacy.note: Apple says it collects Apple Music and Classical usage information for features such as personalized recommendations and release notifications.

catalog.note: Apple says Classical is included with Apple Music and gives access to more than 100 million tracks across the combined subscription.

accessibility.note: Apple says Classical is available on iPhone, iPad, Android and web, wherever Apple Music is offered except Russia and Turkiye.

products.name: Naxos Music Library
products.description: A classical, jazz, world, and educational streaming library often accessed through schools, universities, conservatories, and public libraries.

artist_pay.note: Naxos Music Library is a licensed institutional and personal subscription service, not a direct artist-purchase channel.

openness.note: NML is a streaming library with app and desktop access rather than a DRM-free download store.

privacy.note: Library or institutional access can reduce ad-tech exposure, but privacy depends on the institution and Naxos account path used.

catalog.note: Naxos describes NML as approaching three million classical tracks from more than a thousand labels, with musicologist-authored metadata.

accessibility.note: Naxos says millions can use NML free through institutions such as libraries, universities, conservatories and schools, while individuals can subscribe.

products.name: nugs
products.description: A live-music subscription and store for artist-official concert audio, livestreams, videos, downloads, and CDs.

artist_pay.note: nugs emphasizes artist-official live recordings and lets fans buy shows as downloads, CDs, and other formats.

openness.note: The service is subscription streaming first, but nugs also sells downloads and CDs for some shows without requiring a subscription.

privacy.note: nugs requires accounts and subscription or purchase activity, so it has more behavioral data than buying at a merch table.

catalog.note: nugs says a subscription covers streaming audio from 30,000+ live shows, with new shows added daily and livestream/video access.

accessibility.note: nugs starts at a paid subscription price and runs on web, mobile, Sonos and BluOS, but pay-per-view livestreams may cost extra.

products.name: VEEPS
products.description: A concert livestream and on-demand platform for ticketed and subscription live music, useful when attending in person is not possible.

artist_pay.note: VEEPS sells access to live and on-demand concerts, so support is closer to ticketing than passive background streaming, though platform splits vary.

openness.note: VEEPS is a locked streaming platform for performances, not a download or music-ownership route.

privacy.note: VEEPS requires account and viewing/payment data for concert access, so privacy is weaker than local files or public radio.

catalog.note: VEEPS says All Access provides more than 500 shows per year, but the catalog is live-event-focused rather than all recorded music.

accessibility.note: VEEPS says it offers direct access to live concerts, music and events from anywhere in the world.

products.name: Plexamp
products.description: A polished player for streaming your own Plex-hosted music library across devices, strongest when paired with music you already bought or ripped legally.

artist_pay.note: Plexamp does not itself pay artists; its values benefit depends on whether the listener acquired the music through fair purchases or legal copies.

openness.note: Plex says Plexamp explores your own library and requires Plex Media Server to play personal music content.

privacy.note: Plexamp keeps listening centered on a personal library, but Plex still uses accounts and optional analytics/tracking technologies on its services.

catalog.note: The catalog is whatever music you own or manage in Plex Media Server, not a universal licensed streaming catalog.

accessibility.note: Plexamp is free with many core features, but it requires a Plex Media Server and some features are reserved for Plex Pass.

products.name: Roon
products.description: A paid audiophile library layer that brings local files, selected streaming services, rich metadata, and whole-home playback together.

artist_pay.note: Roon is library/playback software, not a music-rights payment service; artist support comes from the files or linked services the listener uses.

openness.note: Roon says it brings local files and streaming music together while watching local folders without touching the files.

privacy.note: Roon keeps a personal library model, but Valence personalization and service integrations mean it is not a purely offline local player.

catalog.note: Roon imports local files plus favorites from KKBOX, nugs, Qobuz and TIDAL, and includes a live-radio directory.

accessibility.note: Roon lists paid monthly, annual, and lifetime pricing, making it a high-friction option compared with free library tools.

products.name: 7digital
products.description: A broad digital music store for buying DRM-free downloads, useful when you want files you can keep outside a rental app.

artist_pay.note: A download purchase is a clearer paid transaction than a stream, though revenue still flows through labels, distributors and rightsholders.

openness.note: 7digital describes its U.S. store as high-quality DRM-free MP3 music downloads.

privacy.note: Purchasing downloads still requires account and payment data, but owned files can be played later without continuous platform tracking.

catalog.note: 7digital says its catalog includes over 30 million music tracks.

accessibility.note: 7digital lets users browse, buy, preview and download tracks, but regional catalog and store availability can vary.

products.name: Traxsource
products.description: A DJ-oriented download store for house and electronic music, stronger for owned files and niche scenes than for mainstream catalog breadth.

artist_pay.note: Traxsource is a paid download store for tracks, labels and artists, which creates clearer purchase events than passive streaming.

openness.note: Traxsource terms explicitly cover downloadable music files and DJ personal-use performance rights, rather than pure rental streaming.

privacy.note: The store requires account/payment use and is less private than buying records locally or using local files only.

catalog.note: Traxsource is strong in house and electronic genres with labels, artist pages, charts and genre sections, but it is not an all-music catalog.

accessibility.note: The store is easy to browse and buy from online, though it is a niche DJ/download workflow rather than a free streaming app.
